meta.titre: Support and Movement in Animals: antagonistic muscles, tendons and the bending arm

sections.contenu_markdown: A trader in a market carries a heavy basket in front of her chest, then lowers it to the ground and straightens her arms. Every step of this movement depends on bones, muscles and the tough cords that link them. GCE Biology papers often ask which muscle contracts, which one relaxes, and what a tendon really is. This course shows you how to work out the answer each time instead of guessing.

items: Muscle tissue can contract, which means it becomes shorter.
A lever is a rigid bar that turns about a fixed point called a pivot.
The humerus is the bone of the upper arm, while the radius and ulna are the two bones of the forearm.

sections.titre: How the skeleton and muscles produce movement
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Jobs of the skeleton
The skeleton gives the body its shape and **supports** it. It **protects** soft organs: the skull protects the brain and the ribs protect the heart and lungs. It gives muscles something firm to pull on, which allows **movement**. The marrow inside some bones also makes blood cells.

### Parts of a movable joint

| Part | Job |
|---|---|
| Bone | A rigid lever that is moved |
| Muscle | Contracts (shortens) and so pulls on a bone |
| Tendon | A tough, non-elastic cord that joins a muscle to a bone |
| Ligament | A tough, slightly elastic strap that joins one bone to another and holds the joint together |
| Cartilage | A smooth, rubbery layer on the bone ends that lowers friction and absorbs shock |
| Synovial fluid | A liquid that lubricates the joint |

### Antagonistic muscles
A muscle can only **pull**, and only when it contracts. It cannot push. After it stops contracting it relaxes, and it is stretched again by the opposite muscle. Muscles therefore work in **antagonistic pairs**, which pull the same bone in opposite directions. At the elbow the pair is the **biceps** (front of the upper arm) and the **triceps** (back of the upper arm).

| Movement | Biceps | Triceps | Result at the elbow |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bending the arm (flexion) | Contracts | Relaxes | The forearm is pulled up towards the shoulder |
| Straightening the arm (extension) | Relaxes | Contracts | The forearm is pulled down until the arm is straight |

The tendon of the biceps is attached to the radius and the tendon of the triceps to the ulna, so the forearm bones turn like a lever around the elbow, which is a hinge joint. The bones themselves never bend. It is the arm that bends, at the joint.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks you to compare two tough connecting tissues
variantes.contenu_markdown: A tendon connects **muscle to bone**, is tough and does not stretch, so the force of the muscle is passed fully to the bone. A ligament connects **bone to bone**, is tough but slightly elastic, and keeps the joint in place. Neither tendons nor ligaments can contract, because only muscle tissue can contract.

variantes.nom: Support in animals without a bony skeleton
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question mentions an earthworm or an insect
variantes.contenu_markdown: An earthworm has a **hydrostatic skeleton**: fluid in its body is under pressure and supports the body. When the circular muscles contract, the worm becomes long and thin. When the longitudinal muscles contract, it becomes short and fat. Bristles grip the soil so the worm moves forward. An insect has an **exoskeleton**, a hard outer covering that supports and protects the body. It must be shed for the insect to grow.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When each response has to be judged before choosing a letter
variantes.contenu_markdown: Judge every numbered statement on its own as true or false. Write T or F beside each. Only then look for the letter that matches your pattern. Do not let the first statement decide the rest.

sections.enonce_markdown: A boy pulls a bucket of water up from a well by bringing his hands towards his shoulders again and again. (a) Name the muscle of the upper arm that contracts while his arm bends. (b) State what the triceps is doing at that moment. (c) Name the structure that passes the pull of the biceps to the forearm bone. (d) Explain why the biceps alone cannot also straighten his arm when he reaches down for the rope.

etapes.action: Identify the movement in the question.
etapes.justification: Bringing the hand towards the shoulder is a bending movement, which is called flexion at the elbow.

etapes.action: Use the table of antagonistic muscles.
etapes.justification: In bending, the muscle on the front of the upper arm shortens and pulls the forearm up.

etapes.action: Name the link between muscle and bone.
etapes.justification: A muscle is joined to a bone by a tendon, which does not stretch, so the pull reaches the bone.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The tendon of the biceps, attached to the radius.

etapes.action: Explain why a second muscle is needed.
etapes.justification: A muscle can only pull when it contracts. Contracting the biceps again would bend the arm even more, not straighten it.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The triceps must contract to pull the forearm back down.

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) **The biceps**. (b) **The triceps is relaxed** (it is stretched as the arm bends). (c) **The tendon**. (d) A muscle can only pull, never push, so one muscle cannot move a bone in both directions. The arm is straightened when the **triceps contracts and the biceps relaxes**.

items.erreur_markdown: The biceps and the triceps both contract to bend the arm.
items.pourquoi_faux: The two muscles pull in opposite directions. If both contracted, they would work against each other and the arm would stay stiff.
items.correction_markdown: To bend the arm the biceps contracts and the triceps relaxes. To straighten it the triceps contracts and the biceps relaxes.

items.erreur_markdown: The triceps pushes the forearm to straighten the arm.
items.pourquoi_faux: Muscles never push. They only shorten and pull.
items.correction_markdown: The triceps contracts and pulls the ulna, which straightens the arm.

items.erreur_markdown: A tendon is elastic and joins bone to bone.
items.pourquoi_faux: This describes a ligament. A tendon joins muscle to bone and does not stretch.
items.correction_markdown: Tendon: muscle to bone, non-elastic. Ligament: bone to bone, slightly elastic.

items.erreur_markdown: The ulna and the radius bend when the arm bends.
items.pourquoi_faux: Bones are rigid and do not bend. The forearm moves as a whole at the elbow joint.
items.correction_markdown: The forearm bones are pulled by the biceps so that the arm bends at the elbow.

items.erreur_markdown: The only function of the skeleton is support.
items.pourquoi_faux: The skeleton also protects organs, allows movement and, in the marrow of some bones, makes blood cells.
items.correction_markdown: Give at least support, protection and movement when a question asks for functions of the skeleton.

items.enonce_markdown:
ONE or MORE of the responses below is (are) correct.

The skeleton of a mammal

1. Protects the brain by means of the skull.
2. Contains marrow in some bones that makes blood cells.
3. Digests food in the bones.

Choose: A) all three; B) 1 and 2 only; C) 2 and 3 only; D) 1 only.
items.solution_markdown: Judge each statement. 1 is true: the skull encloses the brain. 2 is true: marrow in some bones makes blood cells. 3 is false: bones do not digest food. Statements 1 and 2 only are correct. Answer: **B**.

items.enonce_markdown:
A footballer kicks a ball. His leg swings forward and the knee straightens. The muscles at the front of the thigh (quadriceps) and at the back of the thigh (hamstrings) form an antagonistic pair at the knee.

(a) Which muscle contracts to straighten the knee?
(b) What is the other muscle doing at that moment?
(c) Which muscle contracts to bend the knee when he pulls his leg back?
(d) Name the type of joint at the knee.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The **quadriceps** contracts and pulls the lower leg forward until the knee is straight.
(b) The hamstrings **relax** (they are stretched).
(c) The **hamstrings** contract while the quadriceps relaxes.
(d) A **hinge joint**, which allows movement in one plane like a door hinge.

items.enonce_markdown:
During a match, an athlete tears the tendon that joins his calf muscle to his heel bone.

(a) Explain why the calf muscle can contract but the athlete can no longer raise his heel.
(b) Another player falls and a bone is pulled partly out of its joint. Name the structure that is most likely to be stretched or torn.
(c) State two differences between a tendon and a ligament.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The tendon is the link that transmits the pull of the muscle to the bone. With the tendon torn, the muscle shortens but the pull does not reach the heel bone, so the heel is not raised.
(b) The **ligaments**, because they hold the bones together at the joint.
(c) Any two of: a tendon joins **muscle to bone** while a ligament joins **bone to bone**; a tendon is **non-elastic** while a ligament is slightly elastic; a tendon passes on the pull of a muscle while a ligament holds the joint in place.

items_markdown: A muscle can only pull when it contracts; it never pushes.
Muscles work in antagonistic pairs: bending the arm = biceps contracts, triceps relaxes; straightening = triceps contracts, biceps relaxes.
A tendon joins muscle to bone and does not stretch; a ligament joins bone to bone and is slightly elastic.
Bones do not bend: the arm bends at the elbow joint, a hinge joint.
The skeleton supports, protects, allows movement and its marrow makes blood cells.
